name: Patrick Collison
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Patrick Collison is the cofounder and CEO of Stripe, a company that lets businesses and individuals accept payments over the internet.
Private investors valued Stripe at $159 billion in February 2026.
Patrick and his brother John hatched the idea for Stripe while both were in college in Cambridge at MIT.
Patrick handles engineering and serves as the public face of the company.
An avid reader, Collison keeps hundreds of books on his shelves on topics including physics, feminism and literary criticism.
forbes_facts: The Collison brothers became teenage millionaires in 2008 when they sold their company Auctomatic to Live Current Media for $5 million.
Patrick and John took up coding as kids, competing against each other to master the craft.

name: Terry Gou
forbes_bio: Terry Gou is the founder of Hon Hai Precision Industry, the world's largest electronics contract manufacturer with over 40% market share, whose top customers include Apple.
He stepped down as the firm's chairman in 2019, after 45 years at the helm; he remains at the firm as a director.
Better known by its trade name, Foxconn, Hon Hai employs 900,000 people during peak season.
The company bought Japanese electronics maker Sharp and Nokia's mobile phone brand in 2016.
In 2019, he withdrew his bid to run for the 2020 presidential election, a few months after announcing his intention. Four years later he entered and withdrew from the race for a second time.
forbes_facts: Gou founded the business in 1974 with $7,500 and a belief that electronics products "would be an integral part of everyday life."
Gou met with then-President Donald Trump in 2017 to discuss investing in the U.S., and Trump attended the ground-breaking for a factory in Wisconsin in 2018.

name: Ernesto Bertarelli
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1998-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2019); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Ernesto Bertarelli inherited biotech giant Serono, maker of the multiple sclerosis drug Rebif, following his father's death in 1998.
With his sister Dona, he expanded the company to $2.4 billion in revenues before selling it to Merck for over $13 billion in 2007.
Ernesto and Dona co-chair the Bertarelli Foundation, which focuses on marine conservation and life sciences research.
The family's B-Flexion Group has investments ranging from commercial real estate in London to drug companies.
He also owns the superyacht Vava II.
forbes_facts: Kirsty, Ernesto's wife, is a former Miss UK and a singer-songwriter; she co-wrote a chart-topping song for a British girl group.
A yacht enthusiast, his Team Alinghi won the America's Cup in 2003 and 2007.

name: Lee Boo-jin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Lee Boo-jin is the president and chief executive of Hotel Shilla, one of Seoul's top lodging and conference centers.
Hotel Shilla is also one of the country's biggest duty-free operators.
Lee has also served as an advisor for the trading department of Samsung C&T, her family's de-facto holding company.
Daughter of late Samsung Group patriarch Lee Kun-hee, she  split her father's empire with her mother Hong Ra-hee, brother Jay Y. and sister Seo-hyun.
forbes_facts: She is the eldest daughter of Samsung Chairman Lee Kun-hee and has been nicknamed "little Kun-hee" by the local press for her business acumen.

name: Lin Muqin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Lin Muqin is the chairman and CEO of energy drink maker Eastroc Beverage (Group), which is dual-listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong.
The mogul started out as a technician at a state-owned construction firm, and later found a job at a Shenzhen-based beverage company.
In 1997 he joined Eastroc, then a state-run beverage business, as its vice president. Lin reportedly scraped together more than 4 million yuan ($570,000) to acquire that firm in early 2000s.
He soon focused on making energy drinks. He managed to build Eastroc into China's largest energy drink maker by sales volume partly through offering products at cheaper prices.
Eastroc has diversified into other market segments including coffee and tea-based beverages.

name: Agnete Kirk Thinggaard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: A fourth-generation owner of Lego, Agnete Kirk Thinggaard splits ownership of a 75% stake in the toy company with her father, sister and brother.
Thinggaard also sat on the Lego Foundation's board until 2020, when she stepped down to join family holding company Kirkbi as a board observer.
Her great-grandfather Ole, a carpenter, started making wooden toys in his workshop in 1932 before moving into plastic in the 1940s.
The family also owns about half of theme park operator Merlin Entertainments, which it took private with a consortium in 2019.
Thinggaard represented Denmark in dressage at the Rio de Janeiro Olympics in 2016; she placed 26th in individual competition.

name: Justin Ishbia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Justin Ishbia is the founder and managing partner of Shore Capital Partners, a Chicago-based private equity firm with over $17 billion in assets under management.
The lower middle market focused investment firm has closed over 1,000 control deals in the last 10 years, making it one of the world's most active buyout shops.
In 2025, Ishbia entered into an agreement to become the Chicago White Sox's controlling owner between 2029 and 2034. Forbes estimates he and brother Mat Ishbia already own 35% of the team.
In 2023, the Ishbia brothers bought a majority stake in the NBA's Phoenix Suns and WNBA's Phoenix Mercury in a deal that valued the teams at $4 billion. Mat is the controlling owner.
Justin serves as alternate governor of the Suns, Mercury and Major League Soccer's Nashville SC, in which he owns a minority stake.
He is also a director and owns 19% of mortgage lender UWM holdings, which his father founded in 1986 and his brother Mat now runs. Mat is also a billionaire.
forbes_facts: Justin Ishbia has donated over $10 million to each of his alma maters, Michigan State University and Vanderbilt University Law School.
Prior to joining the investing world, Ishbia worked as an attorney.

name: Bob Parsons
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: The colorful founder of GoDaddy, Bob Parsons, sold off his remaining stake in the web hosting firm and stepped down from the board in 2018.
Parsons grew up "poor as a church mouse" in inner-city Baltimore and struggled in school, flunking the fifth grade.
He sold software firm Parsons Technology to Intuit for $64 million in 1994; three years later he launched Jomax Technologies, later renamed GoDaddy.
In 2014, Parsons founded PXG, which makes high-performance golf equipment and apparel.
He also owns commercial real estate, motorcycle dealerships, a production company and the Scottsdale National Golf Club in Arizona.
Parsons and his wife have given away some $350 million to charities since 2012.
forbes_facts: Parsons says his time as a U.S. Marine in the Vietnam War, where he received a Purple Heart medal and combat action ribbon, has helped him in business.

name: Friede Springer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2002-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Friede Springer inherited a stake in media giant Axel Springer Verlag from her husband, Axel, following his death in 1985.
Hired as the nanny of his two sons, Springer eventually married Axel, who trained her to take over the business.
Among the largest publishing houses in Europe, Axel Springer is active in over 40 countries. Its newspapers include Bild and Die Welt.
The company acquired TV news station N24 (since rebranded as Welt) and the New York-based digital news outlet Business Insider (now renamed Insider) in 2015.
Axel Springer went public in 1985. In 2020, it went private again in a KKR-funded buyout.
forbes_facts: To ensure continuity, in 2020 Friede Springer gave a 15% stake in Axel Springer to CEO Mathias Doepfner and sold him an additional 4.1%.
After the delisting and the gift and sale to Doepfner, she now holds 22.5% of the company.
